scope: Production UI, repository source, previous audits, and pure catalog-function tests. No analyzer installation or example execution. No repository files changed.
summary: Confirmed one category-return defect and four bounded discovery/navigation opportunities. Existing names, aliases, edition-constrained typo recovery, filter recovery, and bookmark restoration work.

findings.title: Returning from a profile or comparison loses the analysis category
findings.reader_task: Inspect or compare tools while retaining a Static/C++ shortlist.
evidence: Live Static analysis + C++ displays 15 of 63 entries at /ToolWiki/static/?language=C%2B%2B.
Open CBMC Read notes. Return to filtered results points to /ToolWiki/?language=C%2B%2B and displays 24 of 89 entries.
Repeat via CBMC and Clang Static Analyzer comparison. Return restores language and both selections but displays 24 of 89 at catalog root.
Category is held in pathname, omitted from allowlisted context, and catalogHref always generates the root route.
findings.impact: The explicit return action silently broadens the shortlist, adding dynamic-only candidates to a static-analysis task.
findings.recommended_change: Carry an allowlisted category in catalog context and map it to the corresponding local category route. Keep existing URL safety constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip All/Static/Dynamic through profiles and comparisons without losing query, form filters, sort or selection.
Unknown category defaults safely; arbitrary URLs and nested context cannot redirect offsite.
findings.compatibility: Additive URL context only; no saved-system format change.

findings.title: The Test an API preset omits existing HTTP API options
findings.reader_task: Use the task shortcut to explore tools for an HTTP API.
evidence: Live Test an API shortcut runs q=API testing and displays three entries: RESTler, Schemathesis and Burp Suite Community Edition.
Changing only the query to HTTP displays five: those three plus Burp Suite Professional and ZAP.
Both omitted profiles already declare HTTP APIs as their target. This finding concerns internal discoverability, not independently reverified product capabilities.
The keyword conjunction matches the literal testing vocabulary unevenly; the shortcut is not an authored task membership set.
findings.impact: Readers using the prominent shortcut miss two already-cataloged HTTP API tools, including the paid counterpart of the displayed manual edition.
findings.recommended_change: Use the existing HTTP context plus Running applications input for the broad preset, and explain schema-generated tests versus manual/security scanning in linked decision guidance. Preserve edition boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: The broad API shortcut includes the five current explicitly HTTP-tagged running-application profiles.
It does not imply that those tools provide equivalent capabilities.
Boofuzz is not automatically included based only on TCP/custom-protocol support.
Add a real-catalog regression for preset membership, avoiding fragile result order assertions.
findings.compatibility: Existing bookmark queries remain valid; the shortcut destination changes.

findings.title: Common taxonomy and documented capability phrases remain absent from catalog vocabulary
findings.reader_task: Find tools by the wiki's own category names or a concrete failure type.
evidence: Live catalog query dynamic analysis returns only capa and FLOSS (2), while the Dynamic category contains 28 entries.
Pure-function query static analysis returns29 while Static category contains63.
Live catalog query null pointer returns0. Full-page search returns4 relevant pages, including Cppcheck and cwe-checker, whose bodies explicitly discuss null pointer findings.
All 132 title/alias queries across89 profiles remain discoverable; the gap is task vocabulary rather than tool names.
findings.impact: A reader can interpret an empty or sparse keyword result as missing tool coverage even when relevant entries already exist.
findings.recommended_change: Index the displayed Static analysis/Dynamic analysis taxonomy labels and add a reviewed, positive capability vocabulary to affected profiles. Retain AND matching and the exclusion of caveats, unsupported features and other-edition claims.
acceptance_criteria: static analysis and dynamic analysis retrieve their corresponding mode populations before other filters.
null pointer retrieves at least the existing profiles whose reviewed positive claims support that term.
Negative scope text and unrelated editions do not become searchable capabilities.
Keep the132 existing title/alias queries and short-language distinctions passing.
dependencies: Primary-source recheck before adding new capability phrases beyond already-supported scope.
findings.compatibility: No URL/schema migration needed; existing optional searchTerms can support profile-specific additions.

findings.title: Empty catalog results do not direct readers to the full-page index
findings.reader_task: Recover when a concept is present in tool notes but not in catalog metadata.
evidence: For null pointer with no filters, the empty state offers fewer search terms and Reset search, but no local action to search full pages.
The separate header Search all pages does find4 pages for the same query.
Search all tools in the empty state only appears to escape an analysis category; it does not invoke Pagefind.
findings.impact: The two-index design is accurate but the recovery path is distant and requires users to know why one search can fail while another succeeds.
findings.recommended_change: Offer an explicit Search all pages for this query action in zero-result recovery, keeping the index distinction visible and preserving the catalog query/filters.
acceptance_criteria: A zero-result capability query can be handed to full-page search without retyping.
Returning to the catalog preserves the original query and filters.
The action is labeled separately from Search all tools, which broadens catalog categories.
Full-page search failure or unavailable development index is explained without silently relaxing catalog filters.
dependencies: Use the existing Starlight/Pagefind search entry point rather than introducing a third search service.

findings.title: Sidebar and in-page category links handle current filters differently
findings.reader_task: Switch from All tools to Static analysis while retaining a current search.
evidence: After restoring q=python type checker, input=Source code, cost=Free and sort=za, the catalog displays2 results (Pyright, mypy).
The in-page Analysis category links carry those query fields.
Clicking the sidebar Static analysis link instead navigates to /ToolWiki/static/ and displays63 of63, clearing all fields.
This is an observed inconsistency, not proof that the site's intended global-navigation convention is wrong.
findings.impact: Two visible links with the same category label produce different search continuity, requiring users to reconstruct constraints.
findings.recommended_change: On catalog pages, synchronize sidebar category links with the same allowlisted filter and comparison context used by in-page tabs. Keep explicit Reset search available.
acceptance_criteria: Within a catalog page, sidebar and in-page links to the same category preserve the same query, filters, sort and selection.
Sidebar navigation from noncatalog pages remains a normal category entry point unless a supported context is available.
Unknown or nested context cannot create an external redirect.
dependencies: Coordinate with SEA-01 category context design.
findings.compatibility: Preserve existing category paths and bookmark URLs.

checks.name: Real-catalog title and alias coverage
checks.details: 132 queries across89 tool titles and aliases; zero missing originating tools.

checks.name: Representative query regression
checks.details: ASan, C sharp, cpp, go, java, python type checker, memory leaks, use after free, race conditions, SBOM, secrets, CVE, symbolic execution exercised. go did not include cargo-audit by substring; java did not include ESLint via JavaScript.

checks.name: Edition-constrained typo correction
checks.details: semgerp + Cost Free offered only Semgrep CE; choosing it retained cost and returned one entry.

checks.name: Filter recovery
checks.details: CodeQL + Free returned no matches and explained one match without filters. Clear filters, keep search retained CodeQL and recovered one result.

checks.name: Full-page search
checks.details: ASan returned4 pages including AddressSanitizer; null pointer returned4 pages. Catalog cards were not returned as a repeated bulk catalog result.

checks.name: Bookmark restoration
checks.details: q=python type checker, input=Source code, cost=Free, sort=za restored two results ordered Pyright then mypy and matching active chips.

checks.name: Cross-category zero-result recovery
checks.details: Static category with HTTP query displayed Search all tools (5 matches).

checks.name: Category return continuity
checks.method: live profile and comparison round trips

prior_audit_reconciliation.evidence: 132 title/alias checks plus representative language queries.
Live Free-constrained Semgrep correction and CodeQL filter recovery pass; Pagefind handoff remains an opportunity.
Four task links exist; API shortcut has SEA-02 membership gap.
SEA-03 shows taxonomy/capability phrases missing despite title/alias completeness.
Form fields survive; pathname category does not. No historical regression timing established.

prior_audit_reconciliation.prior: Useful filter counts, compact list view, platform/integration filters
prior_audit_reconciliation.evidence: Current catalog controls/cards contain no facet counts, list toggle or host/integration filter. Not automatically defects; prioritize by user need.

rejected_leads: Windows, Linux and SARIF return zero catalog results, but the documented index intentionally excludes platform/cost caveats. This is a reviewed metadata/feature opportunity, not a reason to index all prose.
One getByLabel Sort by automation locator timed out; getByRole combobox Sort by succeeded. No product defect inferred.
limitations: Heuristic agent walkthrough, not human usability research.
No external tool capabilities independently reverified; discovery findings compare current metadata and page content.
No performance benchmarks or full accessibility review; dedicated agents cover those areas.
Browser local state only on dedicated audit origin.
